name: Rhythm & Sound
editorial_article: Rhythm & Sound is an iconic Berlin-based music label and project founded by Mark Ernestus and Moritz von Oswald, the masterminds behind the foundational dub-techno output of the 1990s. While their earlier work under monikers like Basic Channel and Maurizio focused on a distinct synthesis of Detroit techno and deep dub-reggae textures, the Rhythm & Sound entity emerged as a purer distillation of their dub-reggae fascination. Throughout the late 1990s and into the 2000s, the label operated as a vehicle for a series of highly influential 10-inch and 12-inch releases that shifted the focus away from the dancefloor-oriented intensity of their earlier techno projects toward a more atmospheric, cavernous, and vocal-led soundscape.\n\nCentral to the label's aesthetic was the frequent collaboration with reggae vocalist Paul St. Hilaire, whose emotive, sparse performances perfectly complemented the duo's heavy, bass-driven production. By stripping back the driving percussion of conventional techno, Rhythm & Sound explored a unique intersection of Jamaican sound-system culture and European minimalist electronic music. The legacy of the label is best captured in seminal compilations like 'Showcase' (1998) and the self-titled 'Rhythm & Sound' (2001). Operating in tandem with the distribution powerhouse Hardwax, the label has remained a cornerstone of underground music culture, maintaining an air of mysterious precision that continues to influence contemporary experimental electronic and dub producers worldwide. Their work serves as a masterclass in tension, silence, and low-frequency resonance, defining the "Berlin dub" sound that has persisted for decades.
editorial_description: The seminal Berlin-based label run by Mark Ernestus and Moritz von Oswald, dedicated to the atmospheric, bass-heavy, and vocal-led fusion of dub-reggae and minimalist electronic music.
